lem-rpm-bmt-transport-algebra:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure supplied by the GR items below. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with its metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, let $c>0$, and let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve parametrized by proper time $\tau$, with $U=D_\tau z$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $F_\tau$ be a continuous alternating two-form along $z$. Define $F^\sharp_\tau$ by
$$g(F^\sharp_\tau(v),w)=F_\tau(w,v).$$
Then $F^\sharp_\tau$ is skew-adjoint with respect to $g$.

For constants $\alpha,a,b\in\mathbb R$, consider the restricted linear transport equations
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left(aF^\sharp(s)+\frac{b}{c^2}U\,\kappa\right),\qquad \kappa:=g(s,F^\sharp(U)).$$
For every initial $s(\tau_0)$ there is a unique solution on each compact subinterval of $I$. Along any such solution,
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(U,s)=\alpha(1-a-b)\kappa.$$
Consequently, the orthogonality constraint $g(U,s)=0$ is preserved when $a+b=1$, and on that constraint $g(s,s)$ is constant. For $\alpha\ne0$, matching the rest-frame spatial law
$$\frac{d\mathbf s}{d\tau}=\alpha G\,(\mathbf s\times\mathbf B)$$
for all spatial $\mathbf s,\mathbf B$, with $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, forces $a=G$ and $b=1-G$. This uniqueness is only within the displayed two-term ansatz; no uniqueness among all covariant spin-transport laws is asserted. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-frame equation does not identify $a$ or $b$.
lem-rpm-body-spin-size-bound:
## Statement

Fix $c>0$ and a future unit observer $n$ in an affine Minkowski spacetime as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. Identify the positive-definite rest space $n^\perp$ with $\mathbb R^3$ and its Euclidean measure $d^3x$. Let $e:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ and $j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be Lebesgue-integrable, both zero almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(0)$ for some $\ell>0$. Suppose $|j(x)|\le e(x)/c$ almost everywhere. Define
$$E_0:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e(x)\,d^3x>0,\qquad M:=E_0/c^2,\qquad \mathbf s_*:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}x\times j(x)\,d^3x.$$
Then $\mathbf s_*$ is absolutely integrable and
$$|\mathbf s_*|\le\ell Mc,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \ell\ge\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc}.$$
The hypotheses are the full mathematical content of this estimate; it is not a bound for a quantum point particle or for a source whose energy density or momentum density fails them.
lem-rpm-charge-multipole-remainder:
## Statement

Let $\ell>0$, $z\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and zero almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(z)$. Write $\|\rho\|_1:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\rho(y)|\,d^3y$. Let $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B_\ell(z)\subset\mathcal U$, and let $b:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^2$ for a finite integer $m\ge1$. For each component $b_k$, let
$$M_k:=\sup_{x\in\overline B_\ell(z)}\|D^2b_k(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty,$$
where the operator norm is taken on the bilinear map using the Euclidean norm in [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Define $Q:=\int\rho\,d^3y$, $d:=\int(y-z)\rho(y)\,d^3y$, and $\mathcal B:=\int\rho(y)b(y)\,d^3y$, with vector integrals taken componentwise. Then
$$\mathcal B_k=Q\,b_k(z)+Db_k(z)d+R_k,\qquad |R_k|\le\frac12M_k\ell^2\|\rho\|_1\quad(k=1,\ldots,m).$$
Thus every fixed component in a smooth finite-component trivialization has the stated charge multipole remainder. A tensor-valued component may be treated only after a fixed smooth trivialization over the ball; derivatives of that trivialization enter $M_k$, and no covariant tensor remainder without this data is asserted.
lem-rpm-flat-centroid-shift:
## Statement

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space, with signature $(-+++)$, and fix $c>0$. Let $p$ be a future timelike vector with rest-frame components $p=(Mc,\mathbf 0)$ for $M>0$. Let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ satisfy the momentum supplementary condition $S^{ab}p_b=0$, and set $s_*^k:=\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}S^{ij}$ in an oriented orthonormal rest-space basis. For every future unit observer
$$n=\gamma(1,\mathbf v/c),\qquad \gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2},\qquad |\mathbf v|<c,$$
define
$$\delta^a:=\frac{S^{ab}n_b}{p\cdot n},\qquad S'^{ab}:=S^{ab}-(\delta^ap^b-\delta^bp^a).$$
Then $p\cdot n\ne0$, $\delta\cdot p=\delta\cdot n=0$, and $S'^{ab}n_b=0$. If the representative point changes by $z\mapsto z+\delta$, the total angular momentum $J=z\wedge p+S$ is unchanged by this stipulated spin-shift rule. In the rest space,
$$\boldsymbol\delta=\frac{\mathbf s_*\times\mathbf v}{Mc^2},$$
If $\mathbf s_*\ne0$, the shifts of all future timelike observers fill the open disk in $\mathbf s_*^\perp$ of radius $|\mathbf s_*|/(Mc)$; the boundary is a supremum and is not attained. If $\mathbf s_*=0$, only the zero shift occurs. This is an exact affine-flat algebraic result.
lem-rpm-ssc-momentum-identity:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice as inherited by the supplied Lorentzian smooth-structure and connection results. Let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline in a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$, parametrized by proper time, with $U=D_\tau z$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $p$ be a $C^1$ vector field along $z$, let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ and $\mathcal T^{ab}=-\mathcal T^{ba}$ be $C^1$ bivector fields along $z$, and let $n$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field along $z$. Suppose
$$S^{ab}n_b=0,\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a+\mathcal T^{ab}.$$
Define $\gamma:=-g(n,U)/c$ and $E_n:=-c\,g(p,n)$. Then $\gamma>0$, and
$$c\gamma\,p^a=\frac{E_n}{c}U^a+S^{ab}D_\tau n_b+\mathcal T^{ab}n_b.$$
Here $\mathcal T$ denotes an arbitrary antisymmetric torque; setting it to zero gives the torque-free case.
lem-rpm-td-local-closure:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and use a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-compatible Levi–Civita connection. Use SI units: coordinates are metres, proper time is seconds, $c>0$ is in metres per second, $p$ is in kilogram metres per second, $S$ is in kilogram metres squared per second, and $R$ has inverse-square-metre components. Let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline parametrized by proper time, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $p$ be a $C^1$ future timelike vector field along $z$, let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ be a $C^1$ bivector field, and suppose the displayed evolution equations hold:

$$D_\tau p^a=f^a:=-\frac12R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.\tag{1}$$

Put $\mu:=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}>0$, $m:=-g(p,U)/c^2>0$, $C^a:=S^{ab}p_b$, and define the linear map

$$K^a{}_b:=\mu^2\delta^a_b-\frac12S^{ac}R_{cbde}S^{de}.$$

At every state where $K$ is invertible and $W:=K^{-1}p$ is future timelike, the TD condition $C=0$ and (1) imply

$$KU=mc^2p,\qquad U=\frac{cW}{\sqrt{-g(W,W)}}.\tag{2}$$

Conversely, on the open state region where $p$ and $W$ are future timelike and $K$ is invertible, the normalized formula for $U$ in (2), together with (1), defines a smooth local ODE. A solution initialized with $C=0$ preserves $C=0$. While it remains in that admissible region, $\mu$ and $S_{ab}S^{ab}/2$ are constant. If $S=0$, then $p=(\mu/c)U$, $D_\tau p=0$, and $D_\tau U=0$. These are local statements; no continuation past loss of invertibility of $K$ or timelikeness of $W$ is asserted. Equations (1) are hypotheses of this mathematical lemma, not a physical derivation of a stress-energy moment model.

def-rpm-body-moments.physical_scope: Definition of flat and local curved stress-energy moments for a smooth compact test body. It supplies moment and transport conventions only; it does not derive MPD equations, a multipole truncation, a matter constitutive law, self-gravity, or an empirical body model.

def-rpm-body-moments:
## Definition

Use the charged/spinning body-model conventions of the now-authored batch-24 carrier [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ in metres, $c>0$, and a $C^2$ future timelike representative curve $z:I\to M$ parametrized by proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The actual supplier defines these quantities and the SI electromagnetic-tensor convention used here. Assume Countable Choice for the GR smooth-structure, convex-normal and parallel-transport suppliers used below.

**(a) Flat isolated-body moments.** In an inertial chart of affine Minkowski space, let $T^{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor with components in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and spatially compact support on every finite time slab. At a fixed time $t$, define
$$p^a(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}T^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\,d^3x,$$
and, for a representative point $z(t)$ on that time slice, define
$$S_z^{ab}(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}\left((x-z(t))^aT^{0b}(ct,\mathbf x)-(x-z(t))^bT^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\right)d^3x.$$
Here $(x-z(t))^0=0$ on the chosen slice, $p$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $S_z$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. These are definitions of moments; no conservation is asserted by clause (a).

**(b) Local curved-body moments.** Let $z\in M$ and let $U_0$ be a convex normal neighborhood containing $z$. Let $\Sigma\subset U_0$ be a spacelike $C^1$ hypersurface through $z$, with future unit normal $n_x$ and induced volume element $d\Sigma$. Let a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor $T^{ab}$ have support on $\Sigma$ compactly contained in $U_0$, with all displayed integrals finite. For each support point $x\in\Sigma$, let $v(x):=\exp_z^{-1}(x)\in T_zM$ be the unique joining position vector supplied by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] and [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $H_{x\to z}:T_xM\to T_zM$ be parallel transport along that unique geodesic, with existence, uniqueness and metric preservation as in [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]. Define $T^\sharp(n_x)^a:=T^{ab}(x)(n_x)_b$ and
$$p_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,\qquad S_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma v(x)\wedge H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,$$
where $(v\wedge w)^{ab}:=v^aw^b-v^bw^a$ and the finite-dimensional vector and tensor integrals are taken componentwise in any basis of $T_zM$. The resulting $p_z$ and $S_z$ are a vector and an antisymmetric tensor at $z$; their units are $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$.

post-rpm-mpd-truncation.physical_scope: Adopted neutral pole-dipole and explicitly closed multipole test-body truncations on a prescribed smooth Lorentzian background. They exclude self-gravity, self-force, arbitrary stress-integral derivation, and any unqualified error or convergence theorem.

post-rpm-mpd-truncation:
## Postulate

Assume Countable Choice as inherited from [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. For a neutral test body, let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve parametrized by proper time, let $U=dz/d\tau$, and let $p^a$ and $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ be the momentum and spin moments of [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. Adopt the pole-dipole evolution equations
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12 R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.$$
A spin-supplementary condition (SSC) is an additional equation $S^{ab}n_b=0$ for a specified future unit timelike field $n$ along $z$; this postulate does not select one SSC, and $p$ is an independently evolved moment rather than a primitive assumption $p=mU$.

For a retained quadrupole or higher-multipole model, adopt
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12 R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd}+f_{\rm extra}^a,\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a+N_{\rm extra}^{ab},$$
where $f_{\rm extra}$ is a specified smooth force map along the state and $N_{\rm extra}^{ab}=-N_{\rm extra}^{ba}$ is a specified smooth torque map. A quadrupole convention that may be adopted is
$$f_{\rm quad}^a=-\frac16J^{bcde}\nabla^aR_{bcde},\qquad N_{\rm quad}^{ab}=\frac43R^{[a}{}_{cde}J^{b]cde},$$
with $J^{bcde}$ satisfying the algebraic symmetries of the curvature tensor, carrying units $\mathrm{kg\,m^4\,s^{-2}}$, and brackets including the factor $1/2$. Any evolved $J$ or higher moment needs its own transport or constitutive law; without it the multipole equations are not a closed initial-value model.

The pole-dipole and multipole equations are adopted finite-dimensional truncations, not derivations from the moment integrals above. Their use as approximations for a material body is restricted to regimes in which its size is small compared with the relevant curvature and background-variation lengths and omitted moment effects are negligible on the stated finite interval. These conditions are qualitative applicability assumptions here: this postulate supplies no uniform error bound, no convergence of truncations, and no global existence claim. No experimental result or measurement is asserted.

pthm-rpm-bmt-constraints.physical_scope: Conditional constraint preservation and restricted-ansatz coefficient matching for the adopted classical BMT polarization model on a prescribed external field. No measured value of the gyromagnetic ratio, quantum-spin derivation, or empirical validation is asserted.

pthm-rpm-bmt-constraints:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Adopt the charged-body quantities and SI tensor convention of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], the polarization transport postulate [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]], and its translational equation obtained from [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. On a local potential domain, assume the finite curve segments are stationary for the adopted action. Let $z$ be a $C^2$ future timelike proper-time curve, $U=dz/d\tau$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, with prescribed continuous alternating field $F$ along it. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $g_s\in\mathbb R$, and an initial $C^1$ spin vector satisfy $g(s,U)=0$. Put $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, and $\kappa=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$. The adopted equations and action result give

$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left[G F^\sharp(s)+(1-G)\frac{U}{c^2}\kappa\right].$$

Then $g(s,U)=0$ and $g(s,s)$ are constant along every solution. In the restricted ansatz $D_\tau s=\alpha[aF^\sharp(s)+bU\kappa/c^2]$, preservation for arbitrary initial data requires $a+b=1$ when $\alpha\ne0$; matching the specified rest-frame law $d\mathbf s/d\tau=\alpha G(\mathbf s\times\mathbf B)$ with $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ then gives $a=G$, $b=1-G$. This coefficient conclusion is only within that ansatz. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-frame matching condition does not identify $a,b$.

pthm-rpm-spherical-charge-size-bound.physical_scope: A conditional static spherical-body energy inequality when its vacuum exterior is exactly Coulomb and its total rest energy includes that exterior field energy plus nonnegative remaining energy. It is not a universal radius theorem for arbitrary charge distributions, and it makes no mass inference for an ideal point charge.

pthm-rpm-spherical-charge-size-bound:
## Statement

Let an extended static spherical charged body have radius $\ell>0$ metres, total charge $q\in\mathbb R$ coulombs, and finite total rest energy $Mc^2$ with $M>0$ kilograms. Use the flat-body moment convention of [[def-rpm-body-moments]] in its rest frame and the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], including $c$ in metres per second and $\varepsilon_0>0$. Its vacuum exterior field is assumed to be exactly
$$\mathbf E(r)=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}\widehat{\mathbf r},\qquad \mathbf B=0,\qquad r\ge\ell.$$
Let $u$ be the vacuum energy density of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] and define $E_{\rm ext}:=\int_{|x|\ge\ell}u(x)\,d^3x$. Assume the total rest energy is the sum of this exterior field energy and a remaining material-plus-interior contribution $E_{\rm rem}\ge0$. Then
$$Mc^2\ge\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\ell},\qquad \ell\ge\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0Mc^2}.$$
The exact Coulomb exterior and nonnegative energy accounting are hypotheses. The theorem does not infer an exterior field from spherical symmetry alone. No identification of field energy with an ideal point particle's rest mass is made.

pthm-rpm-hidden-momentum.physical_scope: Conditional momentum–velocity identities for the adopted neutral pole-dipole test-body equations under Pirani, parallel-observer (OKS), and Tulczyjew–Dixon supplementary conditions. The identity distinguishes the momentum, curve tangent, and observer; no universal identification of momentum with mass times velocity is asserted.

pthm-rpm-hidden-momentum:
## Statement

Assume the neutral pole-dipole equations adopted in [[post-rpm-mpd-truncation]] for the local moments of [[def-rpm-body-moments]]: along a $C^2$ future timelike proper-time curve $z$, with $U=dz/d\tau$, $p$ future timelike and $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$,
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.$$
For any $C^1$ future unit observer field $n$ along the curve satisfying the SSC $S^{ab}n_b=0$, put $\gamma=-g(n,U)/c>0$ and $E_n=-cg(p,n)$. Then
$$c\gamma p^a=\frac{E_n}{c}U^a+S^{ab}D_\tau n_b.$$
In the Pirani branch $n=U/c$, define $m=-g(p,U)/c^2>0$ and $a=D_\tau U$; then
$$p^a=mU^a+\frac{1}{c^2}S^{ab}a_b.$$
In the parallel-observer (OKS) branch $D_\tau n=0$, $p$ is a positive scalar multiple of $U$. In the TD branch $n=p/\mu$, $\mu=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}$, the derivative term generally remains and the identity gives $mc^2p=\mu^2U+S D_\tau p$; it does not by itself imply $p\parallel U$.

pthm-rpm-rest-spin-and-size-bound.physical_scope: Conditional consequences of the adopted classical BMT polarization law in free and uniform-rest-magnetic-field branches, together with separate flat-body centroid and positive-energy size bounds. The BMT polarization vector and body angular-momentum vector are distinct unless an additional identification is explicitly adopted.

pthm-rpm-rest-spin-and-size-bound:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Adopt the charged-body quantities of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the SI field convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the classical BMT law [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]]. For a trajectory stationary under the local action postulate, the translational force equation is supplied by [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. In flat Minkowski spacetime let $m>0$, $q,g_s\in\mathbb R$, $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, and let $U,s$ satisfy
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left[GF^\sharp(s)-(G-1)\frac{U}{c^2}g(s,F^\sharp(U))\right],\qquad g(U,U)=-c^2,\quad g(U,s)=0.$$
The tensor equation is covariant under proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations of the complete field and worldline data. If $F=0$, then $D_\tau U=0$ and $D_\tau s=0$. For any acceleration $a=D_\tau U$ within the Lorentz-force model, the $G=0$ branch is Fermi–Walker transport on the orthogonal spin subspace:
$$D_\tau s=\frac{1}{c^2}\bigl(Ug(a,s)-a g(U,s)\bigr)=\frac{U}{c^2}g(a,s).$$
In an inertial rest frame with uniform $\mathbf E=0$ and constant $\mathbf B\ne0$, $U=(c,\mathbf0)$ is stationary and the $G$ branch has the exact solution
$$\mathbf s(\tau)=\mathbf s_\parallel+\cos(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf s_\perp-\sin(\omega\Delta\tau)\widehat{\mathbf B}\times\mathbf s_\perp,\qquad \omega=\frac{qG}{m}|\mathbf B|,\quad \Delta\tau=\tau-\tau_0,$$
where the projections are parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf B$. The $F=0$, $G=0$, and uniform-field claims are deductions within the adopted model, not experimental statements.

Separately, let a flat body have rest momentum $p=(Mc,\mathbf0)$, $M>0$, antisymmetric angular-momentum tensor with $S^{0i}=0$ (hence $S^{ab}p_b=0$), and Lebesgue-integrable rest densities $e\ge0$ in joules per cubic metre and $j$ in kilogram per square metre per second, supported in a ball of radius $\ell>0$ metres, with $|j|\le e/c$ and $\int e\,d^3x=Mc^2$. Define the body spin $\mathbf s_*:=\int x\times j\,d^3x=\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}S^{ij}\,\mathbf e_k$. Then
$$\ell\ge\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc},\qquad |\boldsymbol\delta|<\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc}$$
for every observer-induced centroid shift $\boldsymbol\delta$ of the flat SSC translation law; the disk radius is a supremum, not an attained boundary for a timelike observer. These rest-body quantities are Lorentz invariant under transforming the complete body data and its momentum-rest hypersurface. No equality between $\mathbf s$ and $\mathbf s_*$ is assumed, so the size inequalities do not bound the BMT polarization unless such an identification is separately adopted.

pthm-rpm-td-invariants.physical_scope: Conditional local consequences of the adopted neutral TD pole-dipole truncation: constant momentum norm and spin-tensor norm on the admissible domain, including the zero-spin geodesic branch. No continuation beyond loss of invertibility or timelikeness, global existence, or empirical adequacy is asserted.

pthm-rpm-td-invariants:
## Statement

Adopt the neutral pole-dipole equations and local body moments of [[post-rpm-mpd-truncation]] and [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. Suppose a solution satisfies the TD condition $S^{ab}p_b=0$, with future timelike $p$, and remains in the local admissible region of [[lem-rpm-td-local-closure]] where $K$ is invertible and $W=K^{-1}p$ is future timelike. Then, on its local interval of existence,
$$\mu:=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}\quad\text{and}\quad \frac12S_{ab}S^{ab}$$
are constant. If the initial spin tensor is zero, it remains zero and the solution obeys
$$p=\frac{\mu}{c}U,\qquad D_\tau p=0,\qquad D_\tau U=0,$$
so the representative curve is a timelike geodesic with constant rest mass $M=\mu/c$. The claims stop if the local TD admissible region ends; no global extension follows.

ex-rpm-bmt-fw-and-g-two.physical_scope: Exact parameter specializations of the adopted classical BMT transport model: $g_s=0$ gives Fermi–Walker transport on the orthogonal spin space, and $g_s=2$ makes the same field generator act on $U$ and $s$. These are model deductions, not measured cases.

ex-rpm-fixed-versus-scaled-charge.physical_scope: Algebraic consequences of the conditional static spherical exterior-energy bound for a fixed-charge point limit and a scaled family with charge and mass tending to zero. No existence of a material family, experimental process, or universal point-particle limit is asserted.

ex-rpm-rest-spin-and-size-bound.physical_scope: A worked exact rest-frame BMT rotation in a uniform magnetic field alongside the separate flat-body SSC centroid disk and positive-energy size bound. The polarization and body angular momentum are kept distinct; no experiment or material family is reported.

ex-rpm-spinless-td.physical_scope: The zero-spin invariant branch of the adopted neutral TD pole-dipole truncation on its local admissible region. It recovers a timelike geodesic with constant rest mass and makes no global-existence or empirical claim.
